intro: You are at Dolmabahçe Palace in İstanbul province, built in 1843–1856 — where the Ottoman court moved after Topkapı. Take in the numbers: 600 metres of façade along the Bosphorus, 285 rooms, and a 4.5-tonne chandelier in the ceremonial hall. This is the scale of the empire's last century.
history: Sultan Abdülmecid found Topkapı inadequate for the diplomacy of the age, so he moved the court to a filled-in bay on the Bosphorus. The Balyan family built the palace between 1843 and 1856: 285 rooms, 46 halls and six hundred metres of quay frontage. In the Republic it became Atatürk's residence and workplace in İstanbul. And it was here that he died, on 10 November 1938.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Ceremonial Hall and the Crystal Staircase, then the Harem apartments. Outside, look for the Clock Tower, and end along the quay and gardens.
facts: Did you know? The palace clocks were stopped at 09:05, the moment of Atatürk's death, and the clock in the room where he died still shows that time. And look up in the ceremonial hall: the four-and-a-half-tonne chandelier hanging from the dome is among the heaviest crystal chandeliers anywhere.
outro: This brings our journey through Dolmabahçe Palace to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave everything untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let these halls keep their quiet for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
